scope: Sytrus first; real-plugin sound design with Surge XT and 3xOsc comparisons
copyright_policy: Short original summaries and source URLs only; no source full texts are stored here.
evidence_rule: Research findings describe their experimental materials and tasks. Parameter mechanics, engineering approximations, practical recipes, and aesthetic judgements are separate claims. Audio features are not listening ground truth.

sources.title: Modeling Noise-Related Timbre Semantic Categories of Orchestral Instrument Sounds With Audio Features, Pitch Register, and Instrument Family
sources.applicability: 153 native-English participants; 156 approximately two-second orchestral single-note stimuli across registers and playing techniques; not a Sytrus patch study.
sources.strength: Strong within the reported stimulus/task domain; moderate for designing hypotheses about new synthesizer sounds.
sources.summary: Raspy/grainy/rough, harsh/noisy, and airy/breathy share some acoustic correlates but differ in feature patterns and meaning. Register, technique, and instrument family matter. Stimuli were loudness-matched before ratings.
operational_impact: Do not translate grainy into one noise/flatness target
Separate airy from harsh noise
Fix register and playback level when comparing
limitations: Ratings and feature prediction are correlations, not a causal recipe
No universal Chinese adjective mapping or aesthetic optimum
No local plugin or listening validation

sources.title: Acoustic and Categorical Dissimilarity of Musical Timbre: Evidence from Asymmetries Between Acoustic and Chimeric Sounds
sources.version: Journal volume/article year 2015; publication date in full-text XML is 2016-01-05
sources.applicability: Dissimilarity, familiarity, and source identification of orchestral recordings and transformed chimeric sounds.
sources.strength: Strong evidence for acoustic and categorical contributions in these experiments; indirect for synth-patch preference.
sources.summary: Acoustic factors alone did not explain all dissimilarity judgements; source categories and familiarity also influenced ratings and agreement. A model using acoustic and categorical descriptors fit better than either alone.
operational_impact: Keep the reference and intended source association
Allow unfamiliar sounds to need different evaluation
Do not use spectral distance as complete timbre similarity
limitations: Does not establish a particular warmth/near/ethereal parameter
Model fit is not a plugin quality score
Results depend on transformed stimuli and comparison task

sources.title: A Taxonomy of Orchestral Grouping Effects Derived from Principles of Auditory Perception
sources.version: Music Theory Online 28.3; issue September 2022, citation metadata gives 2022-10-01; DOI 10.30535/mto.28.3.6
sources.applicability: Auditory grouping, blend, salience, layers, and segmentation in orchestral scores and musical examples.
sources.strength: Well-motivated analytical theory and worked musical examples; not a controlled Sytrus perception experiment.
sources.summary: Concurrent, sequential, and segmental grouping connect timbral properties with musical roles. A fixed instrument combination can blend differently when background material is added; salience also depends on surrounding sounds.
operational_impact: Audition both solo and in a fixed arrangement
Evaluate attack/register/overlap before adding more brightness
Keep foreground/background roles in the design brief
limitations: Analytical predictions are not universal thresholds
Examples are orchestral, not direct plugin settings
Embedded audio was not listened to in this task

sources.title: EBU R 128: Loudness normalisation and permitted maximum level of audio signals
sources.applicability: Broadcast programme loudness and true-peak measurement/normalisation; a useful engineering basis for level-matched comparisons.
sources.strength: Authoritative for its broadcast scope; indirect for short isolated synth sounds.
locators: Footnote 2 on programme duration and LRA
sources.summary: Programme loudness and maximum true peak serve different purposes. Peak normalisation alone leaves loudness differences. R128 uses BS.1770/EBU metering and warns against LRA for programmes shorter than one minute.
operational_impact: Record LUFS separately from peak dBFS and dBTP
Apply post-synthesis gain compensation before A/B
Do not impose -23 LUFS as a patch design optimum
limitations: Does not guarantee perceptual equal loudness for every timbre
Short notes and gating/window choices need explicit handling
Does not prove aesthetic quality

sources.title: Sytrus official online manual
sources.version: Undated live FL Studio online manual, accessed 2026-11-01
sources.applicability: Sytrus operator modifiers, ratio/offset, harmonic editor, envelopes, FM/RM matrix, filter sends, unison, and effects.
sources.strength: Authoritative for documented semantics; not a published private-state schema.
sources.summary: FM/RM rows are modulation targets and columns are sources. Ratio defaults to 2; offset is Hz. Operator volume is automatable and controls modulation from that source. Harmonic amplitudes use a logarithmic UI scale. Individual envelopes need enabling; global ADSR only adjusts existing envelopes. Pluck targets cannot receive FM.
operational_impact: Explicit ratio=1 in init
Directed matrix edges
Enable individual envelope LED
Separate harmonic UI values from linear amplitudes
Keep FM and RM matrices independent
limitations: No reliable mapping from these descriptions to private byte offsets
No local confirmation of every control/version
Does not specify preferred aesthetic values

sources.title: Sytrus Tutorial
sources.version: Undated official-hosted tutorial; credits Eric Mitchell; accessed 2026-11-01
sources.applicability: Minimal subtractive and FM experiments from the Sytrus Default preset.
sources.strength: Direct reproducible plugin instructions; display and parameter mapping still need installed-version checks.
locators: Steps 3.1-3.3 filter routing and envelope activation
sources.summary: From Default, SH=50% yields saw. OP2-column/OP1-row modulates OP1 with OP2. Filtering the modulated sound requires sending OP1, not OP2, into F1. The filter needs input, output, and an enabled cutoff envelope for the corresponding effects.
operational_impact: Use a known Default starting state
Prove static filter route before envelope
Mute direct OP1 output when testing filtered-only output
limitations: SH result depends on reset modifiers and harmonics
Example percentages are demonstrations, not universal timbre optima
No private-state format or CLI interface is documented

sources.title: 3x Osc official online manual
sources.applicability: 3xOsc waveforms, oscillator mixing, phase, stereo detune/pan, HQ and rendering behaviour.
sources.strength: Authoritative for listed controls; exact installed/render behaviour needs local evidence.
sources.summary: Mix controls are sequential ratios: equal three-oscillator mix uses OSC2=50%, OSC3=33%. Phase OFS, stereo detune, pan, and random phase do different things. Non-zero phase starts may click; a short volume attack helps. HQ and render anti-aliasing settings affect comparisons.
operational_impact: Do not assume each oscillator at 33% is equal mix
Check mono when widening
Fix HQ/render settings
Separate intentional texture from clicks
limitations: Controls do not transfer numerically to Sytrus/Surge
Stereo richness is a tutorial description, not a measured quality score
No local audio validation in this task

sources.title: Surge XT User Manual
authors: Surge Synth Team and manual contributors
sources.version: Manual explicitly written for Surge XT 1.3
sources.applicability: Surge XT oscillator/filter routing, filter cutoff, FEG amounts, AEG/FEG ADSR, curve modes, keytrack, filter2 offset, stereo configurations.
sources.strength: Authoritative for 1.3 controls; local 1.4 nightly differs in version.
sources.summary: Cutoff tooltips show Hz and note name. FEG >F1/>F2 depth is required for the filter envelope to influence cutoff. Filter2 offset follows Filter1 including its modulation, envelope and keytrack. Analog/Digital envelope modes have different curves; routing affects waveshaper placement.
operational_impact: Prove filter route before modulation
Record filter configuration and F2 offset
Do not infer physical units from normalized values
Record envelope mode and tempo sync
limitations: Not the same version as installed nightly
No local OSC/audio exercise in this task
Does not establish warmth/ethereal quality

sources.title: Surge XT implementation at the installed nightly commit
authors: Surge Synth Team and repository contributors
sources.applicability: SurgePatch default initialization, semantic OSC parameter paths, OSC dispatch/query architecture.
sources.strength: Direct source evidence at matching short commit; execution/readback still separate.
sources.summary: Initialization has exceptions for global volume/FX bypass and explicitly sets oscillator mutes and envelope internals. Filter semantic addresses include cutoff, resonance, feg_amount, keytrack and offset_mode. Internal floats and parameter types are not automatically physical units.
operational_impact: Use explicit baseline snapshots
Discover and read back semantic controls
Do not send internal time values as seconds
Do not assume init resets every global
limitations: Source inspection is not OSC or audio acceptance
Default initialization is not identical to every factory init patch
No Sytrus state format can be inferred from Surge

sources.title: Sytrus Synth Manual, 2nd Edition
authors: Based on Erik McClure's 2008 Sytrus Synths Creation tutorial, with permission described in the foreword
sources.date_basis: PDF creation/modification metadata; foreword describes August 2016 revision
sources.version: 2nd Edition, 86 pages, FL Studio 12.3 and onwards
sources.applicability: Original/reworked community tutorial with Sytrus exercises, waveform construction, envelope editing, unison, FM/RM and sine harmonics.
sources.strength: Detailed plugin-specific exercises, linked by official manual; older UI and explanatory approximations.
sources.summary: Uses Default and explicitly sets ratio=1 for a controlled tone. Walks through envelope enable, markers, phase/click handling, main ADSR dependencies, directed modulation, and converting shapes into sine-harmonic editing.
operational_impact: Use a controlled dry baseline
Enable actual target envelope
Verify phase/clicks
Keep carrier and modulator roles explicit
limitations: FL12.3-era UI; installed FL26 needs readback
Scope/derivation differs from formal DSP proof
No private-state codec or current CLI support

sources.title: Synth Secrets: What's In A Sound?
sources.version: Synth Secrets Part 1, original Sound On Sound article
sources.applicability: Waveforms, harmonics, and the subtractive-synthesis mechanism.
sources.strength: Clear established mechanism; not a controlled perceptual study.
sources.summary: Subtractive synthesis removes/attenuates parts of harmonically rich sources; waveforms can be understood through harmonic components. Dynamic filtering and envelopes change the sound over time.
operational_impact: Choose rich oscillator before low-pass comparison
Do not expect a low-pass to add missing sine harmonics
Separate source spectrum from downstream processing
limitations: Not a direct mapping of warmth or preference
Simplified pedagogical treatment
No plugin parameter or file format mapping

sources.title: Synth Secrets: Envelopes, Gates & Triggers
sources.applicability: Envelope contours, note gates, triggers, legato and retrigger behaviour.
sources.strength: Useful causal control model; synthesizer examples are older hardware.
sources.summary: ADSR stage values do not fully determine articulation: note gate, trigger/retrigger and reset behaviour alter contours and performance. Attack characteristics can strongly affect instrument identity and punch.
operational_impact: Fix note-off and overlap
Record mono/legato/retrigger
Test short repeated notes as well as sustained chords
limitations: Hardware examples do not numerically map to Sytrus
No universal ideal attack/release
Does not establish near/ethereal as formal metrics

sources.title: Synth Secrets: An Introduction To Frequency Modulation
sources.applicability: Carrier/modulator roles and audio-rate FM sidebands.
sources.strength: Established FM mechanism with worked explanations; plugin implementation details still matter.
sources.summary: Audio-rate frequency modulation creates new spectral components rather than merely slow vibrato. Carrier/modulator frequencies and modulation amount jointly shape the resulting spectrum.
operational_impact: Change ratio and depth separately
Keep modulator out of direct audio while diagnosing FM
Do not call all modulation brightness or noise
limitations: Classic FM equations do not reveal Sytrus private scaling or serialization
Pedagogical examples do not prove an aesthetic optimum
Not local plugin evidence

sources.title: Relating Tuning and Timbre
sources.version: Author-hosted exposition of the Experimental Musical Instruments article; author's introduction links it to the September 1993 JASA paper
sources.applicability: Partial interaction, sensory dissonance models, timbre/tuning relationships and noninteger FM ratios.
sources.strength: Primary author explanation of a concrete model; not a general pleasantness or modern timbre-word study.
sources.summary: Interactions among partials help explain why different spectra suit different tunings and chord relationships. Sensory dissonance is a specific modeled concept; the same patch must be tested on actual intervals/chords.
operational_impact: Test FM ratios in the intended harmony
Separate slow beating, roughness and broadband noise
Do not equate low modeled dissonance with better music
limitations: Summed-partial models omit many musical/contextual effects
Author exposition is used here, not the unread scanned research PDF
No fixed ratio guarantees pleasantness
